newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police step up hunt for Frenchwoman's killer.
newsitem.headline: Irish police step up hunt for Frenchwoman's killer.

text.p: Irish police stepped up a hunt for the killer of the wife of French film producer and critic Daniel Toscan du Plantier on Sunday, saying her assailant may have been bloodstained after bludgeoning her near her remote holiday home.

Police, who said someone might be shielding the murderer of Sophie Toscan du Plantier, 38, issued a fresh appeal to people near the County Cork village of Schull to report anyone with suspicious injuries or bloodied clothing.
The murdered woman was from Ambrax, near Paris. Her husband is a familiar figure at the Cannes film festival.
"We have a few avenues (of inquiry) that we are checking out. We can't say we have a definite suspect yet," Superintendent John Twomey told Reuters by telephone.
Police say the victim, found dead with severe head injuries last Monday four days after flying in for a Christmas visit, had been hit with a blunt instrument in a brutal attack.
"It appears that there was a struggle at the gateway and that the assailant or assailants would be likely to have bloodstains or injuries or marks on them."
Twomey said Irish police might visit France in connection with their inquiries but no decision had yet been taken.

The Dublin-published Sunday Independent said police believe the dead woman was killed by someone who was inside her home. "But they cannot say whether the killer was a guest from France or a local who called and later killed her in a crime of passion," it said.
